text: I played this game way back in 2006 when it first came out and remembered it scaring the crap out of me. Back at that time, horror games were rarely made and were not that famous among most of the gaming community. It had a niche following. However, Monolith made 2 of the greatest horror games at that time which really made more people like me love the genre more. First it was F.E.A.R. and then they made Condemned:Criminal Origins. The game developers took a great risk here. Where F.E.A.R. was basically an action packed shooter with some Japanese horror elements thrown in, Condemned is none of like that. The game focuses more on melee combat than gunning your enemies. You can find all sorts of weapons lying around in your environment like wooden planks, lead pipes, axes and cleavers to bash the hell out of enemies. All the weapons have their own damage, block, range and speed stats making you search different weapons for different situations. There are some guns lying around but you have to search the environment to find them as they are quite well hidden. But they are not as satisfying as breaking skulls, snapping necks and landing punches on enemies. I would recommend to stick with melee for the most fun. The music and atmosphere is very terrifying and scary and I have never been more scared of abandoned buidlings, malls, houses and tunnels but after playing this game they left a huge impression on me. Back in 2006, it was a truly nerve wracking experience. Not to say some of the things which happen in the game are very disturbing. You face enemies which range from drug addicts to other wierd creatures which show up later in the game while occasionally encountering supernatural phenomena. The story for the most part is understandable but later starts to get a little confusing. But I have heard it gets better explained in the sequel. The graphics are dark and depressing which actually matches the themes and undertones of the game. It was not meant to be pretty to look at because the environments which you explore are dull, rusted and abandoned. I played this game again in 2017 and I still find the graphics great. Also, the game workes flawlessly on Windows 10. However, there is a slight audio glitch which is prevalent in Chapter 4 where sounds for some things like kicking doors, running trains amd music may not work properly for you. If that happens there is a steam guide which lets you download a file which fixes it. It only happens in Chapter 4 so its not a big issue. I consider this game a classic horror game and if you like melee combat, scary environents with a convoluted story which will make you scratch your head check this one out. I just wished they ported the sequel to PC as I loved the game and wanted to play the second one as its more terrifying than the original. Buy it !!!! I give it 8 paper cutters out of 10.

title: cook, serve, delicious!
text: When they say 'hardcore', that is not an overstating buzzword. This game is probably the closest any cooking title will ever get to being a Hell's Kitchen simulation. The recipes are simple in execution, but what is not simple is the VOLUME in which you be cooking them. If Cooking Mama was to cooking at home, Cook, Serve, Delicious is to cooking in an environment where your lifestyle is on the line. The game eases you in with some simple difficulty and really easy to make recipes, but as you progress through restaurants in which you're going to be held to a higher standard, so to must you be able to go above and beyond. In case the day to day tedium of completing service days isn't giving you the proper motivation, the game also includes a devious betting system, which dares you complete a chain of perfect orders in a row with specific items on your menu, so no comfort zone here, unless that comfort zone is LITERALLY EVERYTHING. But this game is by no means boring or unfair. Getting perfect days is still possible, but you'll have to manage your money wisely and deal with the ever unpredicatable orders of customers. It's no wonder this game got a sequel. I would recommend this game, but be forewarned, you're going to take a lot of hits until you eventually succeed.
